Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct

1. Record a compact visible-object inventory, including cropped foreground objects, and
   several approximate image landmarks across foreground, subject and background. Image

2. Parameterize camera pose, focal length and shift separately from object dimensions.

   to estimate viewpoint. Compare global framing against local silhouette disagreement.

3. Build a complete economical scene first, with semantic Asset groups, explicit supports,
   major colors and distinctive outlines. Include visible peripheral objects before dense
   textures, stitches or repeated ornaments. Keep all parts of a movable object in its
   hierarchy, so a parent edit moves its upholstery, trim, legs and attachments together.
4. Derive contact heights from supporting geometry and use explicit anchors or bind where
   appropriate. Check contact after rotation or resizing. World AABB contact is approximate:

   treat intended intersections within a constructed part as physical collision failures.

   the largest visible disagreement and revise one main parameter family at a time. Check
   unrelated landmarks and support relations after the change. Preserve successful geometry

6. For an apparently missing object, check construction, unique inclusion keys, hierarchy,

   Presence in a graph does not prove visibility. Absence from a truncated report does not
   prove omission. Do not infer whole-object scale from a probe on a decorative subpart.

Implementation checks grounded in the fixed API:
- All primitive dimensions and radii must be finite and positive. fillet_box requires
  0 < radius <= min(size)/2. For a thin object needing broad planar rounding, compose
  suitable primitives rather than increasing the fillet radius past this limit.
- Rod endpoints must differ; consecutive sweep_tube points must differ.
- include replaces an existing sibling with the same key. Use unique indexed keys in loops.
  It returns the attached node, which can be a clone; retain that returned reference.
- Layout functions and snap return copies. Attach the returned copy before binding it.
- Bind endpoints must already belong to the scene, cannot be ancestor/descendant, and
  dependencies must be acyclic. Supply source_anchor and target_anchor explicitly.
- realize clears Blender. Set camera, lights and bpy materials afterward. If customizing
  the world, first create and assign bpy.data.worlds.new('World') when scene.world is None,

- Semantic inclusion keys name Blender EMPTY markers; primitive mesh children may retain
  names such as Box or Rod. Apply material edits through the semantic group's descendants,
  not a presumed mesh name. Copy shared materials before object-specific modifications.
- Keep construction bounded. Procedural material patterns can represent fine surface detail
  without thousands of separate meshes. Do not change the runner's resource limits.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
The snap and bind calls above explicitly request bottom-to-top placement; their actual
source_anchor defaults are 'center', so do not omit anchors when expressing support.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

import math
import random
import bpy
from sceneact import *

# Visible inventory: brown electronics bench, blue monitor at upper left,
# oscilloscope and power supply below it, keyboard, two meters, calculator,
# black overhead lamp, soldering station, storage drawers, pliers, papers,
# bottles, solder reels, circuit boards, probes, and tangled foreground leads.
# Approximate image landmarks: monitor (20,40)-(178,175), scope (110,163)-(231,228),
# yellow meter (297,154)-(345,244), keyboard (48,248)-(272,350),
# lamp shade (251,66)-(421,113). These are visual estimates.
# World scale is arbitrary. Camera elevation and focal length are uncertain;
# camera parameters are kept separate from all object dimensions.

random.seed(19)
scene = Scene("Electronics workbench")
wood = (.37, .205, .115)
black = (.023, .028, .027)
dark = (.065, .075, .071)
gray = (.48, .49, .44)
cream = (.65, .66, .56)
red = (.60, .018, .012)
yellow = (.94, .61, .015)
silver = (.49, .53, .52)
paper = (.86, .85, .76)

def B(a, key, size, center, color):
    return a.include(key, box(size=size, center=center, color=color))

def R(a, key, radius, start, end, color):
    return a.include(key, rod(radius=radius, start=start, end=end, color=color))

def T(a, key, pts, radius, color):
    return a.include(key, sweep_tube(points=pts, radius=radius, color=color))

def dial(a, key, x, y, z, radius=.016, color=cream):
    R(a, key, radius, (x,y,z), (x,y-.015,z), color)
    B(a, key+"_mark", (.002,.003,radius*.65),
      (x,y-.017,z+radius*.25), dark)

def loop(a, key, center, rx, ry, color, radius=.003, phase=0, n=44):
    cx,cy,cz=center
    points=[]
    for j in range(n+1):
        t=phase+2*math.pi*j/n
        points.append((cx+rx*math.cos(t),cy+ry*math.sin(t),
                       cz+.0025*math.sin(3*t)))
    T(a,key,points,radius,color)

# Architecture and supporting worktop.
room=Asset("Room")
B(room,"wall",(4,.08,3),(0,.86,1.5),(.57,.565,.49))
B(room,"left_wall",(.07,2.4,3),(-1.15,-.25,1.5),(.43,.44,.39))
scene.include("room",room)
desk=Asset("Desk")
B(desk,"wood_top",(2.28,1.66,.065),(0,-.04,.735),wood)
B(desk,"front_edge",(2.28,.035,.09),(0,-.86,.71),(.25,.125,.065))
for x in [-1.02,1.02]:
    B(desk,"leg_"+str(x),(.075,.075,.70),(x,.48,.35),dark)
scene.include("desk",desk)
top=.7675

# Monitor: local assembly with blue display facing the viewer.
monitor=Asset("Monitor")
B(monitor,"foot",(.32,.23,.025),(-.74,.43,top+.013),black)
B(monitor,"pedestal",(.055,.055,.21),(-.74,.48,.88),black)
B(monitor,"housing",(.70,.065,.535),(-.74,.48,1.30),black)
B(monitor,"screen_blue",(.646,.009,.455),(-.74,.442,1.313),(.025,.38,.81))
B(monitor,"screen_upper_glow",(.64,.004,.035),(-.74,.435,1.521),(.12,.65,.94))
B(monitor,"taskbar",(.644,.005,.018),(-.74,.434,1.096),(.015,.19,.60))
B(monitor,"taskbar_light",(.018,.004,.007),(-1.043,.430,1.097),(.44,.77,.86))
# Small login marks in the middle of the screen.
for i in range(2):
    x=-.77+i*.075
    B(monitor,"login_icon_"+str(i),(.019,.004,.020),(x,.431,1.315),
      (.85,.77,.65) if i==0 else (.73,.15,.19))

B(monitor,"brand",(.037,.004,.004),(-.74,.442,1.055),gray)
monitor.turn("z",13,pivot=(-.74,.48,top))
scene.include("monitor",monitor)

# Oscilloscope: cream case, large dark CRT, dense control panel.
scope=Asset("Oscilloscope")
sx,sy=-.43,.30
B(scope,"body",(.55,.29,.285),(sx,sy,top+.151),cream)
B(scope,"front",(.55,.018,.278),(sx,sy-.154,top+.151),(.70,.70,.62))
B(scope,"screen_bezel",(.282,.018,.219),(sx-.112,sy-.17,top+.158),(.35,.38,.34))
B(scope,"screen",(.245,.009,.179),(sx-.112,sy-.183,top+.158),(.075,.105,.10))
for i in range(1,5):
    B(scope,"grid_h_"+str(i),(.235,.001,.0007),(sx-.112,sy-.189,top+.07+i*.033),(.16,.20,.17))
for i in range(1,7):
    B(scope,"grid_v_"+str(i),(.0007,.001,.171),(sx-.235+i*.035,sy-.190,top+.158),(.16,.20,.17))
for row in range(4):
    for col in range(3):

             top+.062+row*.055,.013 if row else .019)
for i in range(6):
    B(scope,"small_button_"+str(i),(.017,.007,.008),
      (sx+.04+i*.028,sy-.182,top+.257),dark)
for x in [sx-.19,sx+.19]:
    B(scope,"foot_"+str(x),(.052,.12,.019),(x,sy,.777),black)
scene.include("oscilloscope",scope)

supply=Asset("Power supply")
B(supply,"case",(.23,.25,.215),(-.91,.26,top+.115),(.40,.43,.36))
B(supply,"face",(.23,.012,.205),(-.91,.129,top+.115),cream)
B(supply,"display_border",(.15,.009,.07),(-.91,.120,top+.163),dark)
B(supply,"display",(.124,.005,.044),(-.91,.113,top+.163),(.16,.22,.18))
for i in range(3):
    dial(supply,"control_"+str(i),-.98+i*.067,.117,top+.067,.022)
B(supply,"top_device",(.16,.14,.045),(-.91,.26,1.015),(.63,.64,.54))
B(supply,"top_display",(.075,.065,.003),(-.91,.245,1.039),dark)
scene.include("power_supply",supply)

# Rear black instrument with colored output terminals and coiled lead.
unit=Asset("Rear black unit")
B(unit,"case",(.34,.22,.13),(.0,.39,top+.07),black)
B(unit,"top",(.32,.20,.013),(.0,.39,top+.14),(.13,.16,.17))
for i,c in enumerate([yellow,silver,silver,red]):
    dial(unit,"terminal_"+str(i),-.115+i*.077,.272,top+.065,.014,c)
loop(unit,"top_cable",(-.02,.39,top+.158),.115,.057,black,.006)
scene.include("rear_instrument",unit)

# Upright yellow multimeter, with all parts tilted together.
meter=Asset("Yellow multimeter")
mx,my=.29,.28
B(meter,"rubber_case",(.205,.067,.365),(mx,my,top+.208),yellow)
B(meter,"front_panel",(.168,.009,.316),(mx,my-.039,top+.217),(.17,.19,.16))
B(meter,"lcd_frame",(.148,.007,.095),(mx,my-.046,top+.315),gray)
B(meter,"lcd",(.128,.004,.065),(mx,my-.051,top+.317),(.39,.46,.37))

      (mx-.045+i*.029,my-.055,top+.322),(.12,.16,.13))
dial(meter,"selector",mx,my-.048,top+.178,.043,black)
R(meter,"selector_stripe",.003,(mx-.008,my-.067,top+.18),
  (mx+.018,my-.067,top+.205),cream)

    dial(meter,"socket_"+str(i),mx-.054+i*.054,my-.048,top+.075,.010,c)
meter.turn("x",-12,pivot=(mx,my,top+.025))
meter.turn("z",-8,pivot=(mx,my,top))
scene.include("yellow_meter",meter)

# Keyboard and calculator in the foreground.
keyboard=Asset("Keyboard")
kx,ky=-.43,-.38
B(keyboard,"base",(.91,.30,.032),(kx,ky,top+.023),(.035,.043,.043))
B(keyboard,"keybed",(.86,.27,.010),(kx,ky,top+.043),(.075,.085,.08))
for row in range(5):
    for col in range(16):
        if row==0 and 4<=col<=8:
            continue
        B(keyboard,f"key_{row}_{col}",(.042,.037,.016),
          (kx-.391+col*.052,ky-.108+row*.052,top+.055),(.018,.024,.024))
        if row>0 and (col+row)%3==0:
            B(keyboard,f"legend_{row}_{col}",(.010,.008,.001),
              (kx-.391+col*.052,ky-.108+row*.052,top+.064),(.43,.46,.43))
B(keyboard,"spacebar",(.245,.036,.016),(kx-.05,ky-.108,top+.055),black)
keyboard.turn("z",15,pivot=(kx,ky,top))
scene.include("keyboard",keyboard)

calc=Asset("Calculator")
cx,cy=-.94,-.65
B(calc,"body",(.18,.285,.027),(cx,cy,top+.025),(.045,.06,.06))
B(calc,"face",(.16,.262,.005),(cx,cy,top+.041),(.63,.65,.58))
B(calc,"lcd",(.126,.055,.003),(cx,cy+.083,top+.045),(.28,.38,.33))
for row in range(6):
    for col in range(4):
        B(calc,f"button_{row}_{col}",(.026,.019,.007),
          (cx-.057+col*.038,cy-.104+row*.029,top+.047),
          (.19,.25,.25) if col<3 else (.28,.39,.42))
calc.turn("z",12,pivot=(cx,cy,top))

# Second handheld meter lying among the leads.
small=Asset("Small handheld meter")
B(small,"body",(.15,.245,.055),(.18,-.285,top+.037),black)

# Back-wall parts drawers, with individual trays and pale label plates.

              (xx,.620,zz-.025),(.29,.31,.28))

# Pinned papers and red-handled pliers on the wall.
wallbits=Asset("Wall tools and papers")
for i in range(3):
    B(wallbits,"paper_"+str(i),(.30,.004,.25),
      (-.01+i*.295,.789,1.36),paper)
    for j in range(5):
